A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TIMI and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices. Existing appendix material can be matched to its relocated counterparts in v2, allowing reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, qualitative generation results, a user study, and component and hyperparameter ablations in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a 500-sample quantitative evaluation and a Trellis backbone comparison in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The ISG separation objective and SGU smoothing, adaptive scaling, and momentum updates remain unchanged. Applying TIMI to Trellis is presented as testing the existing guidance mechanism, without introducing a new algorithmic component or architectural modification.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the stated 3D-Front, real-world, and stylized image coverage. However, v2 does not identify the data source or composition of its new 500-sample and Trellis evaluations, so it is unclear whether represented data coverage changes beyond sample count and backbone.

E2.justification: Trellis, previously discussed as prior work, becomes an evaluated comparator against Trellis + TIMI in v2 Table 9. Hunyuan3D 2.0, DPA, and MIDI remain the comparators in the original benchmark and the new larger evaluation.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a separate 500-sample evaluation beyond the retained 30-scene synthetic benchmark and introduces a controlled Trellis versus Trellis + TIMI comparison. This substantially expands evaluation scale and backbone settings; the original datasets' stated sample counts, metrics, and guidance settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Trellis experiment tests whether TIMI's benefits extend beyond Hunyuan3D 2.0. Existing component and hyperparameter ablations are retained; the qualitative layer-selection and smoothing analyses move from v1 Appendix B into v2 Section 5.3 rather than constituting new analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without uncertainty intervals. v2 introduces 95% confidence intervals for all four methods and all six metrics in Table 8, substantially changing uncertainty reporting for the comparative evaluation. Interval construction, seeds, and repeated-run counts remain unspecified, so additional repeated runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and existing qualitative and user-study results are unchanged. New Table 8 reports TIMI's 500-sample LCD as 0.596 ± 0.023 and SSR as 0.705 ± 0.020, with the best point estimates across all six metrics. Table 9 adds improvements over Trellis, including LCD from 0.692 to 0.635. These are substantial additional results under new settings, not changes to the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same attention formulation, separation loss, update rules, and LCD/SSR definitions. Replacing the prose reference to scaling factor st with lambda_adap aligns notation with the unchanged equation; no mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: training-free multi-instance generation using ISG and SGU, improved spatial fidelity, and efficient inference. The expanded conclusion restates these claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix B interprets the larger evaluation as evidence of reliability beyond a small example set and the Trellis results as evidence of applicability across backbones. It also qualifies absolute performance as dependent on backbone capacity. Existing mechanism explanations and the foundation-model bias caveat remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed Hunyuan3D configuration, Grounded-SAM masks, guided layers and timesteps, smoothing strength, modulation strength, and momentum coefficient are unchanged. The added experiments provide no new implementation instructions, hardware information, or code/data access details.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to SEMV-3D, SAM 3D, and latent diffusion models and modestly revises the related-work discussion. TIMI's positioning remains unchanged. The Ardelean-to-Dogaru/Gen3DSR reference update concerns the same identifiable work rather than a newly introduced comparison method.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and notation corrections, expands related work and the conclusion, and integrates existing appendix ablation discussions into Section 5.3. It also updates author order, affiliations, correspondence and publication information, and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8 and 9 and relocates v1's appendix Figures 9 and 10 into the main text as Figures 7 and 10. Existing figures retain their visual evidence, with associated renumbering, expanded captions, and table/page reflow rather than substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: The 500-sample comparison, confidence intervals, and Trellis test strengthen empirical support beyond v1's small main benchmark and single evaluated backbone. However, the new tests' data provenance and detailed settings, and the interval estimation procedure, remain unspecified. Table 8's substantially overlapping intervals also leave comparative significance unresolved. The additions provide a useful but limited overall quality improvement.
